question: The ampere magnitude is determined by setting the numerical value of the elementary charge equal to _______ .
solution:
The correct answer is __**1.602176634 x 10⁻¹⁹ C**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The elementary charge is the charge of a single electron or proton, and its value has been precisely defined as **1.602176634 x 10⁻¹⁹ coulombs (C)**.
 
• This value is an important constant in physics and chemistry, used in defining the ampere based on the International System of Units (SI).
 
• The definition of the ampere relies on fixing the numerical value of the elementary charge to **exactly 1.602176634 x 10⁻¹⁹ C**.
 
• This constant is established by the International Committee for Weights and Measures (CIPM) and is part of the updated SI system introduced in 2019.
 
• The elementary charge plays a critical role in understanding electromagnetic phenomena and is integral to equations in quantum mechanics and electrodynamics.
